full_judgment: 7. Mr TH Khan along with Mr. Sk. Hassan Arif, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner on referring to the judgment of the Courts below submits that the learned Assistant judge after elaborate discussion of the evidences on record clearly found that the story of surrender as put forward by the plaintiff was not being successfully proved in Court by the plaintiff and that the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 did not have any authority to lease out the suit land in favour of the plaintiff twice for self same land and thus dismissed the suit rightly but the appellate Court without at all reversing the said material findings of the trial Court allowed the appeal arbitrarily and accordingly it was not a proper judgment of reversal under Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submits that there may be thousands of defects in the defendants case but for the same, the plaintiffs will not get a decree, he is required to prove his own independent case. In the instant case the plaintiff contended that the original allottee Tozammel Hossain surrendered the suit land in favour of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 in lieu of a plot in the Mohammadpur Housing Society. Under section 68 of the Evidence Act, the plaintiff is required to prove the validity as well as legality of the story of surrender but the plaintiff has totally failed to prove the story of surrender by adducing sufficient material witnesses. He then further submits that at present, there is no provision for surrender in any law. Lastly on showing the deposition of one Nuruzzaman deposing in Court on behalf of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 supporting the plaintiffs case and stated that "document of surrender is lying with the record in their office" but the said document was not been brought before the Court in order to prove the plaintiffs contention, thus in view of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act the defendant will get the benefit about the presumption that if the document is placed before the Court, it will speak, otherwise not supporting the plaintiffs case and, as such, it was not been placed before the Court. Considering this aspect of the case, the learned Assistant judge has correctly found that the alleged story of surrender as claimed by the plaintiff was not been proved but the appellate Court has failed to consider that aspect of the case and accordingly the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside.
